SMTO-RST-0020 — Your change wasn't saved because the data changed at the same time

GUID: a07523c9-4782-5c06-8e50-08cab0c7c34d
Slug: runtime-revision-conflict
Domain: RST · Subsystem: runtime

What happened

  • SMTO tried to save a change, but the same item was changed, deleted or busy at that moment, so this change was not saved. Results from earlier work are kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Refresh the page so you see the current version of the item you were changing. Someone or something else changed it at the same moment, so your screen was out of date.
  2. Check whether the item still exists and whether your change is already there. The item may have been deleted, or another window may already have made the same change.
  3. Close other browser tabs or windows showing the same item, and wait for any task using it to finish. Two places changing the same item at once is what causes this conflict.
  4. Make your change again once, on the refreshed page. Once the screen shows the latest version, SMTO can save the change safely.

What success looks like

  • After refreshing, your change saves and stays in place when you reload the page.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, and mention what you were changing. Don't keep repeating an action that sends messages or changes other systems until you've confirmed it didn't already happen.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A runtime-state transaction was rejected because its expected revision or owner epoch was stale, the record was deleted, an ownership/uniqueness rule conflicted, or contention persisted after bounded retries.

What this means

  • Transaction/repository publication detects a stale revision or epoch, deleted record, conflicting ownership/uniqueness or concurrent read/index change. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • Transaction/repository publication detects a stale revision or epoch, deleted record, conflicting ownership/uniqueness or concurrent read/index change.

How to diagnose it

  • Reload the relevant exact records and distinguish revision conflict from a tombstone or duplicate identity.

How to fix it

  • Reload the affected record (conversation, parameter, schedule, workflow run or model-output capture) and confirm the operation still applies before resubmitting with the current revision. RevisionConflict comes from runtime_state/hub.py; TransactionContention means the hub could not publish within bounded retries, so check for another tab, task or client writing the same record.
  • Reload the current state and confirm that the requested operation is still applicable before trying again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate applicable operation commits under current ownership and revision constraints.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
